Social Media Policy
POLICY FOR PARTICIPATION ON ALL OFFICIAL SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS MANAGED BY THE OFFICE OF SENATOR AMANDA M. CAPPELLETTI
This Page is maintained by the official Senate Office of State Senator Amanda M. Cappelletti (“Office”). The purpose of this page and all pages managed by the Office are to inform the general public on policies, legislation, events, activities, and other useful information from the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, the Counties of Montgomery and Delaware, the Office of Senator Cappelletti, and the 17th Senatorial District. Any person who interacts with any social media page managed by the Office consents to the terms of this policy.
Use of this Page to post content that is unrelated to the official purpose for which the Office is utilizing the Page is prohibited. Additionally, the following user actions are prohibited: Ethnic and racial slurs, profanity, personal insults, spam, or material that is harassing, defamatory, fraudulent, sexually explicit, or discriminatory under federal, state or local law. Posts related to election campaigns or commercial activity will be removed.
Comments in violation of this policy will be removed. Users found in violation of this policy may have their ability to comment or interact with this page suspended, revoked or limited.
We urge all users to please be respectful toward others.

title: Internship Program
raw_text:
Internship Program
Interning for a state senator is an excellent way to learn about the legislative process, state government, and constituent services. The office of Senator Amanda M. Cappelletti is committed to serving the people of Pennsylvania and advancing meaningful policies for our community. In an effort to increase civic education, provide young people with work experience opportunities in state government, and engage with our community, we offer the following internship programs available throughout the year.
Summer Internship Program
Application window:
March 20 to April 20
Our Summer intern program currently focuses on opportunities with the Communications, Legislative, and Constituents Services Departments in our office.
Fall Internship Program
Application window:
July 20 to August 20
Our Fall intern program focuses on opportunities with the Communications and Legislative Departments in our office. In our Fall Internship program, we do not accept Constituent Services Intern Applications.
Spring Internship Program
Application window:
October 20 to November 20
Our Spring intern program currently focuses on opportunities with the Communications, Legislative, and Constituent Services Departments in our office.
Application Guidelines:
Please submit the following to
Cappelletti@PASenate.com
with the subject line “[Type of Internship] Internship Application – [Your Name]”:
A resume outlining your relevant experience.
A brief cover letter (1 page max) explaining why you’re interested in this internship and how your skills align with the role.
If applying for a legislative or communications internship, please provide a writing sample (e.g., a blog post, press release, social media post, or any relevant content).
Legislative Internship
Position Overview:
Policy/Legal interns will support the work of Senator Cappelletti’s legislative team by assisting in policy development and research, preparation for legislative session, compiling stakeholder feedback on legislation, and writing a policy paper. This internship offers a unique opportunity to gain firsthand experience at the intersection of state government, public policy, and civic engagement.
Key Responsibilities:
Conduct legal research on emerging issues that are of interest to the legislative team.
Draft policy briefs, talking points, and memos for legislative staff and the Senator.
Assist with tracking legislation and attending relevant committee hearings or briefings on behalf of the Senator.
Participate in meetings with stakeholders, advocacy groups, and government agencies.
Complete a policy research project at the direction of the Legislative team on a policy issue that is relevant to the student.
Qualifications:
Current or rising college junior or senior, or JD, MPA, MPP, or related graduate program.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
Interest in public service, Pennsylvania state government, and progressive policy.
Strong research and policy analysis skills.
Familiarity with Pennsylvania legislative process or a strong interest in learning.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and general office technology.
Additional Information
Flexible scheduling is available to accommodate other commitments.
This internship may include evening or weekend work to attend certain events.
Communications Internship
We are looking for a highly motivated Communications Intern to join our team. This internship offers a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in political communications, with a focus on social media, writing press materials, and speechwriting. Graphic design experience is preferred, as you’ll help create compelling visuals to amplify our message.
Key Responsibilities:
Social Media Management:
Assist in managing the Senator’s social media presence, including content creation, monitoring engagement, and tracking analytics.
Press Materials:
Help write press releases, statements, talking points, and other materials for the media.
Speechwriting:
Support the drafting of speeches, talking points, and remarks for the Senator at public events.
Graphic Design:
Assist in creating graphics, infographics, and other visual content for social media, websites, and public communications. Experience with Canva is a plus.
Research:
Conduct research on policy issues, media trends, and public opinion to inform communications strategies.
Event Support:
Help with promoting public events hosted by the office.
Preferred Qualifications:
Graphic Design Experience Preferred:
Familiarity with Canva is preferred. You will be expected to assist with creating visual content.
Strong Writing Skills:
Must be able to write clearly and concisely in various formats, from social media posts to speeches and press releases.
Social Media Savvy:
Experience managing or contributing to social media accounts on platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter/Threads/or Bluesky (personal accounts qualify).
Interest in Politics:
A passion for public service and an interest in local or state politics is strongly encouraged.
Attention to Detail:
Ability to work quickly and accurately while adhering to deadlines.
Team Player:
Strong communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
Requirements:
Currently enrolled in a degree program in Communications, Political Science, Public Relations, Journalism, or a related field.
Previous internship or volunteer experience in communications, media, or political campaigns is a plus but not required.
Ability to work 15 hours per week with some remote flexibility.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), familiarity with social media platforms, and design tools.
Constituent Services Internship
The Constituent Services Intern plays a key support role in the Senator’ Cappelletti’s office by assisting with day-to-day communications with constituents and helping the district team address community concerns. This internship provides a hands-on opportunity to learn about public service, government operations, and community engagement through meaningful, service-oriented work.
Key Responsibilities:
Answer phones and assist with incoming constituent inquiries via phone, email, and walk-ins.
Support the Constituent Services team in researching and responding to constituent issues, including inquiries related to state agencies and local services.
Assist in processing applications for commendations, proclamations, and constituent services.
Help maintain constituent files and update casework logs and databases.
Participate in small-scale research or outreach projects related to constituent priorities.
Attend and staff community events, town halls, and meetings as a representative of the Senator’s office.
Provide general office support, including data entry, mailings, and document preparation.
Monitor local news and community updates relevant to the district.
Support special projects or legislative outreach efforts as needed.
Qualifications:
Current college student or recent graduate interested in public service, political science, communications, or a related field.
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
Friendly, professional demeanor with strong interpersonal skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and general office technology.
Interest in state government, policy, and community engagement.
Bilingual in Spanish is a plus.
Additional Information:
Flexible scheduling is available to accommodate academic commitments.
Internship may include occasional evening or weekend work for community events.
This is a learning opportunity; academic credit may be available depending on school policy.

title: The Economy and Jobs
raw_text:
PA Senate Democrats
FOR EVERY PENNSYLVANIAN
ECONOMY AND JOBS
The last three years have been unprecedented. The pandemic, political upheaval, inflation, and international conflict have all had their toll on the national economy and our own pocketbooks. We can do more to help all Pennsylvanians by implementing popular and proven programs and policies.
INCREASE THE MINIMUM WAGE
Governor Shapiro has proposed an immediate increase to Pennsylvania’s minimum wage to $15 an hour and we stand with him! The old adage that a rising tide lifts all ships still holds true. An increase to $15 would directly benefit nearly 1.5 million workers, or 25 percent of Pennsylvania workers.
Especially during times of inflation, we must increase the purchasing power of wage-earning Pennsylvanians. Prior to this inflationary period, the minimum had lost 30 percent of its purchasing power compared to 50 years ago. This is unacceptable in an economy as strong as ours. We must pass Senate Bill 12 in this legislative session.
INVEST FEDERAL IIJA AND IRA MONEY WISELY
The Pennsylvania Legislature and Governor worked in a bipartisan fashion to thoughtfully and strategically invest the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding last year. We made historic investments in housing, front line worker recruitment and retention, juvenile and adult mental health programming, and law enforcement and community violence programs. We can do this again with the massive funding coming from the federal government for infrastructure and energy investments.
FIGHT INFLATION AND PUT PEOPLE OVER PROFITS
It’s clear that a rebounding economy and tight labor markets are causing inflation in the US economy, but big business is taking advantage of the crisis to jack up prices and hit record profits on the backs of consumers. We must protect people from corporate inflation by cracking down on price gouging, promoting greater competition in the marketplace, and supporting small businesses and regional supply chains over international interests. We must fight inflation by eliminating the scarcity of essential commodities that all people have a right to – housing, energy, and transportation – by building 21st century infrastructure for Americans.
It’s time to:
Build more middle-class housing
Build our energy sector away from volatile global fossil fuel markets by investing in renewable energy
Bring down prescription drug prices and reign in healthcare costs
Prevent corporate consolidation through strong anti-trust enforcement
Protect Americans from Price Gouging
PUBLIC SECTOR OSHA COVERAGE
Not all workers in Pennsylvania are treated equally. Our caucus intends to resolve this inequity. The Occupational Health and Safety Act, commonly referred to as OSHA, covers private sector employees and provides safety and health standards in the workplace and enforcement mechanisms to ensure the law is followed. However, public sector employees in Pennsylvania are not provided the same protections as private sector employees and we want that to change. We intend to change this by providing state level OSHA protections for public sector employees.
MANDATE EARNED SICK LEAVE
Healthy employees are productive employees. We need to ensure that people have time off to take care of themselves and their families. Choosing between a paycheck and going to the doctor shouldn’t be a choice at all. In addition to the benefits for employees, earned sick leave leads to fewer sick days for the overall workforce, less turnover, better use of preventive care, and higher workplace productivity.
END THE PAY GAP
In 2021, women earned 82% of what men earned, according to the U.S. Government Accountability Office analysis of median hourly earnings of both full- and part-time workers. Based on this estimate, it would take an extra 42 days of work for women to earn what men did in 2020.
In recent years, the pay gap was considerably greater for women in most historically underserved racial and ethnic groups than for White women, according to the Census Bureau’s published ACS data on full-time workers. For example, for every dollar earned by White men in 2021:
Black or African American women earned an estimated 63 cents (a pay gap of 37 cents on the dollar);
Hispanic or Latina women earned an estimated 58 cents (a pay gap of 42 cents on the dollar);
White women earned an estimated 79 cents (a pay gap of 21 cents on the dollar); and
Asian women earned an estimated 97 cents (a pay gap of 3 cents on the dollar).
We must adopt policies that eliminate the pay gap and lift up the income of all women.
INVEST IN EMPLOYEES
Under our plan the state will provide programs and training to improve the income and conditions of workers. Customized job training, connecting community colleges and technical schools with employers, improving worker investment board resources, creating career readiness councils are at the top of our agenda. Improving paychecks, benefits, and working environment is the heart of the Senate Democrats’ priorities.
Providing access to high quality childcare will go a long way to providing parents job opportunities that may be unmanageable otherwise. Our caucus is advocating for an increase of $66.7 million for Child Care Services in the 2023-24 budget, so that up to 75,000 low-income families will continue to be enrolled in a subsidized child care program through the Child Care Works Program.
Availability of high-quality public transit provides access to higher paying jobs, increases worker productivity, and protects family budgets by reducing vehicle and transportation costs. When coupled with transit-oriented development (development occurring within a half miles of transit access) transit reduces traffic, infrastructure costs, and improves local efficiency. The Senate Democrats are ardent supporters of state funding for regional mass transit systems.
END WORKPLACE HARASSMENT, RACISM AND SEXUAL ABUSE
We must empower people in the workplace. Providing safe and equal working conditions is the first step. We will not stand for a person’s job or promotion to be leveraged for sex. We will not stand for a person’s livelihood to be taken away from them because they reported workplace harassment.
ENCOURAGE SMALL BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT AND GROWTH
Small businesses improve the economy from the ground up, create new jobs, and build wealth at the community level. We must foster an environment that provides small and diverse businesses with opportunities to be establish and grow that have been previously unattainable. Focused small business loans, access to capital for growth, technical assistance, and employee training support are on the Senate Democrat agenda.
PROVIDE INCENTIVES TO EXISTING BUSINESSES
Whether it’s to attract national or multi-national corporations, or provide that last bit of financing for a mid-size company to grow, we must help provide the competitive advantage necessary for Pennsylvania to be business friendly. We have worked hard to make our tax climate more business friendly including reducing the Corporate Net Income Tax in half over the next few years; we have provided many tax credits and exemptions to attract and retain companies, but we plan to do more to grow our business community.
INCENTIVIZE MANUFACTURING
Tax credits and grants to support the most critical sector of Pennsylvania’s past and future will ensure a productive economy with family sustaining jobs. Whether it’s making sure companies have the capital to grow or the pipeline to find skilled employees, we must make sure that the Commonwealth is doing all it can to support our manufacturing industry.
STABILIZE AND GROW DISTRESSED COMMUNITIES
Many of our cities and larger municipalities are continuing to struggle with budget deficits and debt, aging infrastructure, and stagnant economies. The Senate Democrats plans for the larger economy will go a long way toward turning these trends around. We will also help these communities fight blight by investing in demolition, rehabilitation, and rebuilding, providing technical assistance for budgeting and financing, providing local tax relief through property tax reform, and strengthen local school districts.
PROVIDE ACCESS TO AFFORDABLE AND HEALTHY HOUSING
The Pennsylvania Senate Democrat have consistently stood for the creation of affordable and accessible housing. We’ve successfully fought for the creation and increase of funding to the Pennsylvania Housing Affordability Trust Fund. Additionally, we are pushing for a state low-income housing tax credit to improve the impact of the existing and successful federal credit. In Pennsylvania, for every $10 million in affordable housing construction, it will generate $19.6 million in total economic impact and support 110 jobs. With an economic multiplier effect of nearly 2 and the jobs supported, the impact of building and renovating affordable housing is important to the Pennsylvania economy.
PROVIDE A STATE SOCIAL SECURITY RETIREMENT SUPPLEMENT
Social Security is falling short and the state can step up and help. We should create a state managed retirement fund to supplement the retirement income provided by social security.

PA Senate Democrats
FOR EVERY PENNSYLVANIAN
Quality, Affordable Healthcare
The last three years have been unprecedented. The pandemic, political upheaval, inflation, and international conflict have all had their toll on the national economy and our own pocketbooks. We can do more to help all Pennsylvanians by implementing popular and proven programs and policies.
HEALTHCARE
Reforming our health care system and government response to public health – we must restore public trust through meaningful, systemic change that directly benefits the public, erases inequities in service and availability, and adequately provides resources from state government to address basic tenets of good health effectively and proactively across all communities.
Health care is a human right. Therefore, ALL individuals should have access to high-quality, affordable health care. We support a public option so that everyone has access to the health care they need regardless of their ability to work.

Mental health care must be addressed. We have made historic investment in juvenile, school based care, and adult mental health care in the last year, but we must make this an annual expenditure and do more to help all Pennsylvanians.
We must provide equitable access to care for minority communities.
Continue to support the Affordable Care Act. It’s essential that the pillars of the ACA are kept in place, including:
Maintaining coverage of essential health benefits including protecting Medicaid
Covering pre-existing conditions; and
Prohibiting lifetime and annual benefit limits
We must invest in community care, including community health clinics to provide healthcare in minority and working-class neighborhoods
Ensure state and county health offices are adequately staffed, properly trained, and held to high levels of transparency and accountability to the public
Continued support and reliable funding for county human services block grants
HUMAN SERVICES
Providing Access to Public Health Supports and Services Across the Entire Lifespan
Maintain the right to abortion and reproductive health care access for all women
Make childcare accessible and affordable to all working families
Improve access to and affordability of housing and provide annual funding for the Whole Homes program
Support childcare workers and providers by providing living wages and adequate reimbursement rates

Support legislative solutions that recognize social determinants of health and alleviate burdens of economically disadvantaged and health-vulnerable populations

Food insecurity is a major barrier to good health over an individual’s lifespan, and we must do more at the state level to combat it
We have to work to end the public benefits cliff. No one should be penalized for making more money and trying to improve their lot in life. We must find ways to extend coverage on important state programs for those increasing their incomes just above means tested income levels.
Several pandemic era programs are ending at the federal level, including SNAP and Medicaid emergency programs. We need to find solutions for the impacted populations, including providing state funding for the lost federal appropriations.

title: Safe Communities
raw_text:
PA Senate Democrats
FOR EVERY PENNSYLVANIAN
COMMUNITY VIOLENCE PREVENTION
The list of impacted cities to mass shootings in now too long to list. And community violence is increasing as homicides by firearms have been on the rise for many years and according to the CDC there were 1,752 firearm mortalities in Pennsylvania in 2020. That’s up from 1,390 in 2014.
Endless community violence, suicides and massacres need to be answered by state action. We need to keep dangerous weapons off the streets and out of the hands of people that are unstable and likely to commit deadly crimes, provide more and improved mental health services, and provide resources to secure vulnerable sites like schools and places of worship.
In the recent legislative sessions, we acted to address some safety concerns related to school and community violence and to protect victims of domestic violence. We adopted legislation requiring schools to conduct safety and security assessment and provided $200 million in grants to provide mental health resources and secure school building. We further provided $260 million for grants to support law enforcement, gun violence prevention and prosecution, develop community violence prevention programs.
But in order to truly address gun violence the General Assembly needs to do more. We will fight for the following:
BAN ASSAULT WEAPONS
We must prohibit ownership of assault weapons such as the AR-15, including its high capacity ammunition feeding devices and other accessories, have become the tool of choice in mass murders.
EXTREME RISK PROTECTIONS
Implementation of legislation to allow for courts to order public protection orders if a person is demonstrating dangerous mental health characteristics would provide much needed protection to the public. Such an order would temporarily suspend an individual’s access to firearms if there is documented evidence that a person is threatening to harm themselves or others. The person subject to that order must surrender their guns to police and will not be able to buy, sell, or possess other firearms with a judge determining the time frame of this suspension not to exceed one year.
SAFE STORAGE REQUIREMENTS
Too many firearm incidents happen because of improperly securing guns to prevent them from getting into the wrong hands, including children or unwell individuals. Requiring gun locks and safe storage are commonsense prevention options.
MENTAL HEALTH IN SCHOOLS
Recognizing the particular vulnerability that exists in our schools, we propose a new requirement that each school must provide school psychologists, school counselors, and school social workers to meet the mental health needs of their students. Offering these services will go a long way toward intervening with students that might commit the worst violence and to greatly improve school climate and student performance.
UNIVERSAL BACKGROUND CHECKS
While this should be common sense, expanded our current system of background checks to ALL firearm sales has been elusive. Currently certain gun show purchases and person-to-person sales do not require a basic background check. Every firearm sale in Pennsylvania needs to undergo a background check.
The time for debate has passed. It’s clear that guns are a problem that needs to be addressed and without legislation we are going to continue to see the awful events of the past repeat themselves. We must take action now.
EQUALITY AND SOCIAL JUSTICE
Pennsylvania can be a wonderful place to work and live, to raise a family, to go to school, to start a business. We must ensure that those opportunities are available to all our residents, regardless of their gender, race, sexual orientation or creed.
We must fight racism in all its forms and in all its places. Hate crimes are skyrocketing, racism is rampant in our politics and our institutions, and it has become normalized by right-wing elected officials and pundits. This must come to an end as we seek justice for all. Expanding and better enforcing our hate crimes statute, recognizing and rooting racism in our institutions, better training for law enforcement, and a focus on post-secondary schools for both educating our citizens and ensuring fair access to an education are just some of the ideas we are embracing.
This means preserving women’s rights, making sure their access to health care and reproductive rights are protected, that they receive the same pay for the same work, and that they are free from sexual harassment in the workplace.
We need to protect the rights of our LGBTQ citizens as well. Right now, we have no statewide nondiscrimination laws that prohibit discrimination in housing or employment based on sexual orientation or gender. Many of our neighboring states do, and it’s time we join them in making everyone feel comfortable and welcome in this commonwealth.
Providing the LGBT community same protections against hate crimes afforded to other minority groups. Many of our neighboring states do, and it’s time we join them in making everyone feel safe and welcome in this Commonwealth
CRIMINAL JUSTICE REFORM
Re-entering a community after serving time in prison can be difficult, and it’s one of the factors that leads to higher rates of recidivism. We can:
Reform our probation and parole systems to reduce the total amount of time a person can be on probation or parole, eliminate or reduce the impact of technical violations, and reduce the power that prosecutors and judges have for prolonging terms for getting out of probation and parole.
Create programs to ease the re-entry process can be enormously helpful in getting a person back on their feet
Continue to reform the expungement process, so that more minor offenses can be wiped from a person’s record so they don’t spend the rest of their lives paying for a single mistake.
“Ban the Box,” a provision that prohibits employers from asking job applicants if they’ve ever been convicted of a crime in the first round of their screening process. Too often, checking “Yes” in that box will automatically disqualify an applicant.
Eliminate incarceration for someone who fails to pay their cash bail. Paying a cash bail is simply not possible for some people and locking them up for failing to pay that is a policy that punishes them again for not having means.

Education

EDUCATION
We have accomplished a lot toward providing more funding to public school over the past eight years, But, as the Fair Funding court case rightly points out, we have a lot more to do. Educational opportunities should not be determined by a zip code – ALL students deserve access to high-quality education regardless of where they live, what they look like, or how they learn. Commit to fund schools at the state level

Utilize the Fair Funding Formula
Address the teacher and school personnel shortage by providing school district with the resources to retrain and recruit staff to ensure a high quality education.

Expand career and technical training

CTE and job training programs will meet demands of new economy (including the post-COVID, technology-related job losses)

Work with the private sector to design customized job training opportunities
Reform charter schools so that they meet the same rigorous standards that our traditional public school districts must attain

The College Grants
I often receive calls regarding financial aid for students. Fortunately, there are many options available to Pennsylanians pursuing higher education. Please see below for information on both federal and state assistance programs available to students.
Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency
PHEAA helps students access loans, grants, and scholarships.  While PHEAA is currently not lending from its own funds, it maintains its commitment to assisting students find loans.  Visit their website to learn more,
www.pheaa.org
.
Federal Student Aid
There are many programs for Federal Student Aid available which can be found at
www.Studentaid.ed.gov
or by contacting the
Federal Student Aid Information Center
at 1-800-433-3243.  To learn the amount and the type of Federal Student Aid you qualify for, you should fill out a Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA), which can be found at
www.fafsa.ed.gov
.
Here are examples of common Federal student aid programs:
Stafford Loans
:  This includes Federal Direct Loans, as well as Federal Family Education Loans (FFEL), which may be subsidized or unsubsidized by the Federal Government. In a Federal Direct loan, the funds come directly from the Federal Government, where in the FFEL program, the funds will come through a private bank, credit union, or other lending agency.  On a subsidized loan, you do not have to pay any interest while you are enrolled at least half time, and your principal will be deferred.  Unsubsidized loans will accrue interest as would a typical loan.
Federal PLUS loans:
Also part of the Stafford Loan program, these are unsubsidized loans available to parents of dependent undergraduate students, or to graduate students and are available through the Federal Family Education Loan Program and the Federal Direct Loan Program.
Pell Grants:
Need-based grants that do not have to be repaid.
Work-Study:
Wage-Subsidized positions at the school which will allow you to earn money to pay for your education while you study.   The Student Educational Employment program offers positions with the Federal Government to qualifying students.  This can be accessed at
www.usajobs.gov/Help/working-in-government/unique-hiring-paths/students/
.
Also search the
Catalog of Federal Domestic Assistance
for other grants, scholarships, and fellowships.
After applying, you should keep copies of all forms and correspondence as you must reapply each year. Not every school participates in each program. You should contact your school’s financial aid department to learn about the program in which they participate.
Financial Aid Department at Your College
The school you have chosen may have its own student aid programs including merit and need-based scholarships.  You should contact your Financial Aid Department to determine what aid they can offer.
Private Scholarships
There exist an incredible number of privately sponsored scholarships, for some of which you may be eligible.  Often these may be difficult to find.  If you go to
www.pheaa.com
, they can help you find some of the scholarships for which you may be eligible.  You should speak with local community groups and religious institutions, as well as your high school guidance counselor, to learn of other scholarships that may be available.
Repaying Loans
Help is available for
repaying your loans
.
Loan Consolidation:
Federal loans can be consolidated once, with some exceptions.  While simplifying the management of your loans, loan consolidation in general can lead to a significantly lower, fixed interest rate, decreasing your overall expenses.  To learn more about this, please visit
http://loanconsolidation.ed.gov/
.
Private loans often are able to be consolidated, depending on your individual loan agreement.  You should consult your lender to be sure this option is available to you.

Volunteers who complete one year of service receive an education award for current higher education expenses or to repay student loans.

title: Pennsylvania Senators, Advocates, Rally in Harrisburg for Access to Contraceptives
raw_text:
Pennsylvania Senators, Advocates, Rally in Harrisburg for Access to Contraceptives
September 28, 2026
Harrisburg, PA − September 28, 2026 –
This morning,
Senator Amanda M. Cappelletti
(D-17, Montgomery/Delaware),
Senator Maria Collett
(D-12, Montgomery), and
Senator Judy Schwank
(D-11, Berks), rallied with First Lady Lori Shapiro, Pennsylvania House colleagues, national experts, and Planned Parenthood advocates to
call for action on
Senate Bill 1112
.
The legislation would require all insurers to provide coverage for contraceptives, eliminate most co-payments for related coverage, remove pre-authorization requirements for certain contraceptives, and authorize insurers to cover up to 12 months of birth control at one time.
“The reproductive healthcare landscape right now is a scary place for Americans,”
said Senator Cappelletti, Co-Chair of the Pennsylvania Women’s Health Caucus.
“The federal government has made it clear they are willing to go to extreme lengths to threaten our access to care. Pennsylvania must respond to show our communities we will protect their health and wellbeing when other officials in Washington are too busy buying into conspiracy theories.”
Following the
Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization
Supreme Court ruling
, nationwide threats to family planning clinics have increased. Prior to
Dobbs
,
publicly funded family planning clinics provided contraceptive care to one quarter of all U.S. women receiving such care
. Many of these clinics have been forced to close their doors, or struggle to operate as the Trump administration withholds
Title X
and
Medicaid
funding. The Republican Federal Spending Bill—H.R. 1—passed in 2025 has
posed additional threats to Medicaid
, which covers FDA-approved contraceptives for people in all 50 states.
“Americans across the political spectrum agree that people should be able to access contraception and decide for themselves whether and when to start or grow a family,” said
Dana Singiser, co-founder of the Contraceptive Access Initiative
. “At a moment when misinformation about contraception is increasingly driving the national debate, it has never been more important that people have accurate information, real access to the methods that are right for them, insurance coverage for over-the-counter contraception and clarity about their rights. I’m grateful to Pennsylvania’s leaders for shining a light on an issue that matters to families across the Commonwealth and the country.”
Contraceptives offer a variety of uses. While they are commonly used to prevent unintended pregnancies, forms of contraceptives serve a number of medical purposes, often including hormone regulation, family planning, and treatment for severe conditions like endometriosis, dysmenorrhea, and Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (previously known as PCOS).
“While out-of-touch rightwing politicians continue to threaten our essential healthcare freedoms, we gathered today to share a clear message: we will not back down in our fight to protect and expand Pennsylvanians’ access to contraceptives,”
said Senator Maria Collett.
“Our colleagues in the House have taken action. The question now is whether or not Senate Republicans have the courage and the common sense to stand with the majority of Pennsylvanians who agree that birth control access should not be a partisan issue.”
The Pennsylvania House of Representatives has already taken steps to protect access to contraceptives.
Representative Mary Jo Daley (D-168, Montgomery)
has introduced
House Bill 2605
, which would prohibit the Commonwealth from interfering with the use of medically appropriate methods of contraception or fertility treatments. In May 2025, the House also voted 116-87 in support of Representative Leanne Krueger’s (D-161, Delaware)
House Bill 1140
, companion legislation to SB 1112.
“House Democrats have been working hard to champion contraceptive access for all Pennsylvanians by passing bills that protect our right to full reproductive healthcare. This includes HB1140, which has passed the House two sessions in a row with bipartisan support, but the Senate has failed to move the bill,”
said Representative Leanne Krueger.
“With a federal government that is openly hostile to reproductive rights, we must enshrine protections in state law to ensure access to contraceptives, safeguard privacy, and remove barriers to essential reproductive health tools. This is the time for action.”
House Bill 1140 has been stalled in the Senate Banking and Insurance committee since June 3, 2025. The committee is chaired by Republican Senator Chris Gebhard.
“All women in this Commonwealth should have access to full reproductive healthcare, and that includes access to contraception,” s
aid Representative Gina H. Curry, (D-164, Delaware), who co-sponsored House Bill 1140 and serves a co-chair of the Pennsylvania Women’s Health Caucus.
“This is about agency—the power to make decisions about our own bodies, our families and our futures. Women deserve the freedom to determine if and when motherhood is part of their journey and to have access to the healthcare that makes that choice real. When cost, geography or other systemic barriers stand in the way, they limit not only healthcare, but opportunity. Reproductive equity means removing those barriers so every woman has the power and resources to determine the course of her own life and family.”
Governor Josh Shapiro has continued to fight for Pennsylvanians to have access to the full spectrum of reproductive healthcare, and polling shows
strong bipartisan support for increasing access to contraception.
After decisive action in the House, Senate Democrats, advocates, and partners are calling on the Senate Republican majority to finally send these bills to the Governor’s desk.
“Access to quality health care is something every woman deserves, but we know that in some communities access to health care can be a real challenge, especially for women in rural communities,”
said First Lady Lori Shapiro.
“Contraceptives play an essential role in women’s health care and making sure they are accessible is just plain common sense.”
“A lack of access to contraception affects every Pennsylvanian, whether we realize it or not. We have an opportunity to follow the example set in the House of Representatives and advance legislation that protects access to essential reproductive health care,”
said Senator Schwank.
“Ensuring that all Pennsylvanians can obtain the contraception they need to live healthy lives is good policy and the right thing to do.”
The full list of speakers from the September 28 press conference included:
Senator Amanda M. Cappelletti,
Senate District 17
Representative Leanne Krueger,
House District 161
Representative Gina H. Curry,
House District 164
Dana Singiser,
Co-founder of the Contraceptive Access Initiative and former special assistant to President Obama
Senator Maria Collett,
Senate District 12
First Lady Lori Shapiro
Lizz Bender,
Advocate with Planned Parenthood
Senator Judy Schwank,
Senate District 11

title: Senator Cappelletti Hosts Forum at SCI Phoenix, Authors Memo to Create Pathways to Geriatric and Medical Parole in Pa.

Senator Cappelletti Hosts Forum at SCI Phoenix, Authors Memo to Create Pathways to Geriatric and Medical Parole in Pa.
August 26, 2026
Montgomery County, PA
–
August 26, 2026
– Pennsylvania State Senator Amanda M. Cappelletti (D-17 Montgomery/Delaware) hosted a “Geriatric Parole Forum” on Tuesday, August 25 at the State Correctional Institution – Phoenix (SCI Phoenix), welcoming nearly 150 guests to the facility’s chapel.
The forum included two panel discussions. The first discussion featured voices from the incarcerated population at SCI Phoenix, where three men shared their stories before a panel of state legislators and advocated for parole pathways for aging and infirmed incarcerated people. Following their testimony was a conversation among Pennsylvania General Assembly members, leaders from the Pennsylvania Department of Human Services, and criminal justice experts, about potential legislative options for geriatric parole and compassionate medical release in the Commonwealth.
“Nearly half of all states already provide options for geriatric or medical parole. And with more than 11,000 incarcerated people now qualifying as geriatric, we know just how financially burdensome it is for Pennsylvania’s prison system to continue to house and care for this rapidly growing population,”
said Senator Cappelletti, Democratic Chair for the Pennsylvania Senate Judiciary Committee.
“Yesterday’s conversation provided us with a space to gather a diverse range of input so our legislature can craft comprehensive legislation that best serves our Commonwealth. Now is the time for Pennsylvania to adapt a responsible, evidence-based approach.”
The Case for Geriatric and Medical Parole Options
According to
research conducted by Families Against Mandatory Minimums
(FAMM), arrests drop steeply by the time people are in their early thirties, and almost three-quarters of arrests are of people below the age of 40. Similar trends are seen with recidivism rates, which
The United States Sentencing Commission
corroborates, citing that the recidivism rate of older offenders (21.3%) was less than half that of offenders under the age of 50 (53.4%).
“Incarcerated elders, people who are debilitated or incapacitated, and those nearing death are the most expensive and burdensome to incarcerate and the least likely to reoffend. It is sound and humane correctional policy to provide pathways to release for them,”
said Mary Price, Senior Counsel at FAAM.
These statistics have reined true in communities where aging populations were resentenced or released back into their communities.
A 2020 study monitored 174 people
who were resentenced and released in Philadelphia after the Supreme Court of the United States ruled that juveniles receiving life sentences was unconstitutional.
After nearly two years being in their communities, only two individuals were reconvicted of any offense.
Following the famous
Unger v. State
case, 200 people serving life without parole in Maryland were released after serving 40 or more years. All of those released were originally convicted of a violent crime, and
97%
did not recidivate upon release.
Maryland is one of at least 23 states (and the District of Columbia) that now provides options for geriatric and medical parole. The bill—
Senate Bill 181
,
sponsored by
Maryland Senator Shelly Hettleman (D-11, Baltimore)
—passed the Maryland Senate last year 35-12, and the Maryland House at 104-36.
“Geriatric and medical parole reform is smart criminal justice policy. In Maryland, we recognized that we could keep our communities safe at the same time that we could target our limited resources more effectively,”
said Senator Hettleman.
“By releasing those who have severe medical needs that cannot be addressed in our carceral system, or who are older and have been incarcerated for substantial periods of time, we are using our public resources more humanely and more efficiently. We look forward to Pennsylvania joining Maryland in these actions.”
Keith Wallington, Senior Campaign Strategist at The Sentencing Project, was instrumental in helping get SB181 signed into law.
“Prior to SB181, geriatric parole simply didn’t work in Maryland. In a state fraught with racial disparities, geriatric parole reform was needed to address an aging population in Maryland’s legal system that disproportionately impacted people of color,”
Wallington said.
Wallington said the success of SB181 can be attributed to the courage of the Ungers and returning citizens who testified and shared their stories, Senator Hettleman’s strong sponsorship, and collaboration between the Maryland Office of the Public Defender, the Office of the Attorney General, and the Maryland Equal Justice Collaborative.
“Pennsylvania now has the opportunity to achieve similar results through intentional partnership between legislators, advocates and experts across the criminal justice system,”
Wallington said.
The Way Forward in Pennsylvania
In response to the testimonies from fellow General Assembly members, incarcerated individuals, and outside experts,
Senator Cappelletti released a memo with Senator Sharif Street (D-3, Philadelphia) to the Pennsylvania Senate
following the Forum with her intent to introduce legislation tackling this issue. Senator Cappelletti has also been proud to support bills to expand parole options, including Senator Street’s
Senate Bill 135
and
Senate Bill 136
.
“Today I ask you to consider whether Pennsylvania can protect its citizens while also recognizing that mercy, accountability, and common sense can exist together,”
said Craig Datesman, an incarcerated individual, during his remarks at the forum.
Datesman is 73 years old and has been incarcerated for 44 years.
Datesman has been denied commutation
—despite the support of the victim’s family and his rehabilitation—and continues to serve his life sentence.
“History will remember not only that we punished crime, but we had the courage to recognize rehabilitation, exercise sound judgement, and pursue justice with both strength and compassion,”
Datesman said in closing.
In the Pennsylvania House, Representative Johanny Cepeda-Freytiz (D-129, Berks) is a co-sponsor of
House Bill 1550
which would create a pathway to parole for incarcerated people aged 50 and older, who have served the lesser of 25 years in prison or one-half of their minimum sentence.
“Geriatric parole would provide support for our corrections system and those who the system has helped to redeem. Legislative collaboration between the House and Senate is a major step to ensuring a pathway to parole is possible in Pennsylvania,”
said Representative Cepeda-Freytiz.
“I am grateful to Senator Cappelletti for her work in bringing this legislation to the Senate, and I look forward to continuing our collaboration to help this measure become law.”
Senator Cappelletti wrote in her memo that her legislation intends to provide a data driven, humane, and fiscally responsible solution to a crisis that is already burdening Pennsylvania’s carceral system.
“The evidence is overwhelming, and the human and financial costs of doing nothing are undeniable. Here in Pennsylvania, we have a responsibility to care for
every
Pennsylvanian—no matter their community, or their past. We all deserve a second chance,”
said Senator Cappelletti
. “We’ve seen similar legislation succeed in our neighboring states. This Commonwealth must now come together—across chambers, agencies, and across the aisle—to implement meaningful change for aging and infirmed incarcerated people.”

,

title: Approaching 120 Days: Senators Jay Costa and Amanda M. Cappelletti Address the Legislature’s Responsibility to Respond to Commonwealth v. Lee
raw_text:
Approaching 120 Days: Senators Jay Costa and Amanda M. Cappelletti Address the Legislature’s Responsibility to Respond to Commonwealth v. Lee
July 23, 2026
Harrisburg – July 23, 2026 –
The Pennsylvania Supreme Court deemed mandatory life sentences for people convicted of second-degree felony murder unconstitutional on March 26, 2026. The landmark Court ruling was then stayed, giving the Pennsylvania General Assembly 120 days to amend the unconstitutional law and provide an alternative remedy for the more than 1,100 incarcerated individuals who have been harshly or unfairly convicted.
The legislature is now out of time, with the Court’s mandated deadline approaching on Friday, July 24.
Senate Democratic Leader Jay Costa (D-43, Allegheny)
and
Senator Amanda M. Cappelletti, Democratic Chair of the Senate Judiciary Committee (D-17, Delaware/Montgomery)
, issued the following statement:
“The Court’s ruling in
Commonwealth v. Lee
gave our state legislature a historic opportunity to redress a longstanding injustice. Pennsylvania is one of only four states that mandate life-without-parole sentences for people who are convicted of second-degree felony murder. Such sentences do not consider whether the actor intended to take a life when they committed the felony. Nor do they consider their degree of involvement in the crime. At its core, the way Pennsylvania was sentencing those convicted of felony murder was often disproportionate with the crimes at hand, and found to be “cruel punishment” under the Pennsylvania Constitution.
“The legislature
has known
about the July 24 deadline to heed the Court’s ruling. Rather than take action to deliver a just, fair solution to incarcerated Pennsylvanians serving these sentences, Pennsylvania Senate Republicans have spent the past 120 days spewing misinformation about what this ruling means for public safety, while refusing to work collaboratively.
“Though Senate Republicans are content stoking the dishonest lie that the more than 1,100 people serving these sentences will be released from prison come July 24, the truth is that if the legislature fails to act, resentencings are the actual expected outcome. Individual resentencings will take
years
to process. And it is likely that many incarcerated people impacted by this ruling may still receive a life sentence. Resentencings require the full use of our court system, which will severely strain our public defenders and prosecutors, and produce inconsistent outcomes across the state.
“It is also true that Senate Republicans claimed to take action by passing
Senate Bill 1400
back in June. However, not only did Senate Republicans proceed without feedback, they shirked participating in ongoing conversations among stakeholders who were working to craft a comprehensive solution. Instead of working in a bipartisan way, they circulated their proposed legislation less than 24 hours before a Senate Judiciary Committee vote, without any stakeholder or Democratic feedback, to force a perfunctory measure through the chamber. In our divided legislature, when bipartisan consensus is essential, these performative measures are unacceptable.
“A true solution to this matter would provide an adequate sentence for second-degree felony murder that is appropriate under Pennsylvania’s current sentencing guidelines and proportionate to the role the actor played in the crime; parole eligibility for people currently serving a life-without-parole sentence for felony murder after they’ve served a minimum number of years and; a procedure that ensures a judge will issue a culpability determination if they impose a life-without-parole sentence.
“We, along with our Senate Democratic colleagues, look forward to passing collaborative, comprehensive, and meaningful legislation that actually delivers justice.”

Delco Delegation Announces State RACP Grant Funding for Main Line Health Emergency Care Expansion
July 17, 2026
$4 Million Public Investment Begins Rebuilding Emergency Care in Delaware County After Private Equity’s Decisions Led to the Collapse of the Crozer Health System
DELAWARE COUNTY, PA – July 17, 2026
– Members of the Delaware County Delegation announced today that $4 million in Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program (RACP) grant funding has been awarded to Main Line Health to support the expansion of its emergency care capacity, a critical step toward stabilizing emergency care access in Delaware County.
Main Line Health — including Riddle Hospital, Paoli Hospital, Lankenau Medical Center, and Bryn Mawr Hospital — has absorbed a significant and unsustainable surge in emergency department volume after the collapse of Crozer Health.
“This $4 million investment is an important next step in rebuilding the robust emergency-care network Delaware County lost when Prospect Medical Holdings — a private-equity company whose business model prioritized profit over care — dismantled Crozer Health’s emergency departments and left many of our residents without the services they depended on,” Senator Tim Kearney (D-26) said. “This investment allows Main Line Health to restore — and strengthen — the lifesaving care residents rely on when every minute matters.”
Since Crozer’s collapse, Main Line Health’s hospitals — along with Mercy Fitzgerald — have stepped up to cover a far wider footprint than they were intended to serve, absorbing emergency department volume from communities that suddenly lost local access to care. This shift has forced residents and ambulances into longer drives and longer transport times, stretching these facilities thin and underscoring the strain created when private equity eliminated emergency care options across southern Delco.
“My district was hit hard by the closure of Crozer Chester, especially families in communities like Chester, Upland, Trainer, Brookhaven, Marcus Hook, and Eddystone, to name a few,” said Senator John Kane (D-9). “I’m grateful to Main Line Health — and to Mercy Fitzgerald — for stepping up when emergency care disappeared, and I’m encouraged to see this investment support an expanded emergency care facility within Main Line Health’s system. Wherever the final site is located, this expansion will improve access for families who have been left without nearby emergency care options.”
“Private equity created this crisis, and the damage they caused can’t be undone,” added Rep. Lisa Borowski (D-168). “But this $4 million public investment gives Main Line Health the footing to start rebuilding emergency care access after Prospect walked away. I drafted House Bill 1460 — the Health System Protection Act — to block private-equity firms from causing further harm to Pennsylvanians by requiring real oversight and establishing financial guardrails for our health care system. Until then, using state funds to expand existing emergency care facilities is one of the most effective ways we can save lives and help Main Line Health advance the plan to restore the care that so many families depend on.”
“Since the devastating closure of the Crozer Health system at the hands of private equity, Main Line Health has had to fill in the gaps and do more with less for thousands of patients in need,” said Senator Amanda M. Cappelletti (D-17). “This funding ensures they can continue moving forward and providing quality care for our neighbors.”
To meet the needs of patients displaced by Crozer’s collapse, the expanded facility at an as-yet determined site will feature a full‑service outpatient emergency department with treatment bays, CT scanners, general radiology rooms, an ultrasound room, an outpatient laboratory, and MRI capabilities, giving Main Line Health the diagnostic and treatment capacity needed to serve the region effectively.
“A modern emergency department with treatment bays and advanced imaging is exactly what our residents have needed since Crozer’s collapse,” said Rep. Heather Boyd (D-163). “CT scanners, radiology, and ultrasound capacity will help families get answers quickly when every minute matters.”
“Bringing MRI capabilities and an expanded diagnostic capacity to Main Line Health’s emergency care system is a major step toward restoring the emergency-care foundation our county lost,” said Rep. Gina Curry (D-164). “These upgrades will help Main Line Health respond more effectively when patients arrive in crisis.”
It will also house primary care and family medicine services, and provide specialized treatment for trauma, heart attack, stroke, and minor injuries and illnesses. Funding will support construction, state-of-the-art equipment, and the infrastructure needed to ensure patients have timely access to high-quality, efficient, and lifesaving care.
“Specialized treatment for trauma, heart attack, and stroke is essential for communities that were left without viable emergency departments,” said Rep. Carol Kazeem (D-159). “This expansion brings back critical services southern Delaware County residents have been missing for far too long.”
“Adding an outpatient lab and modern imaging capabilities will make a real difference for people who can’t wait for diagnostics,” said Rep. Jennifer O’Mara (D-165). “Main Line Health has absorbed enormous patient volume, and these improvements will help Main Line Health deliver faster, more reliable care.”
“State-of-the-art equipment and modern infrastructure are essential for delivering high-quality, efficient care,” said Rep. Leanne Krueger (D-161). “This investment ensures Main Line Health can meet the increased needs of patients displaced by the loss of Crozer’s emergency departments.”
“For many working families in my district, losing Crozer’s emergency departments meant longer drives, longer waits, and fewer real options,” said Rep. David Delloso (D‑162). “This investment helps Main Line Health expand the capacity needed to bring care closer to home and reduce the strain on residents who can’t afford delays when a medical crisis hits. Prospect Medical caused irreparable damage, both in job loss and in routine medical care. Returning emergency services is just step one.”
“We are incredibly grateful to Governor Shapiro and the Delaware County legislative delegation for this investment in the health of our community,” said Ed Jimenez, President and CEO, Main Line Health. “These funds will help us strengthen access to high-quality care close to home and ensure we can continue meeting the evolving needs of our patients.”
“On behalf of the Delaware County delegation, I want to thank Governor Shapiro for recognizing the urgency of restoring emergency-care access in our communities,” said Senator Anthony Hardy Williams (D-8). “This public investment gives Main Line Health the support needed to rebuild a system families can depend on.”
As planning and construction continues, the delegation looks forward to seeing Main Line Health’s vision take shape and deliver the modern, accessible emergency care system Delaware County deserves.

Lawmakers Launch New Kids & Families Caucus
October 14, 2026
Joined by Lieutenant Governor Davis and Allegheny County Executive Innamorato, state legislators unveil new bicameral caucus focused on supporting children and families
Plum, PA – October 14, 2026 −
State
Senator Nick Pisciottano
(D-45, Allegheny) and State Representatives
Aerion Abney
(D-19, Allegheny) and
Jennifer O’Mara
(D-165, Delaware) were joined by
Lieutenant Governor Austin Davis
,
Allegheny County Executive Sara Innamorato
, and local officials Wednesday at the Sampson Family YMCA in Plum to announce the formation of the Pennsylvania General Assembly’s new
Kids & Families Caucus
.
Pisciottano, Abney, and O’Mara will serve as co-chairs of the caucus along with State
Senator Amanda Cappelletti
(D-17, Delaware/Montgomery). Lieutenant Governor Davis and County Executive Innamorato highlighted the importance of supporting children and families at every level of government, from local communities to county and state leadership.
The new bicameral caucus will bring together lawmakers from the Senate and House of Representatives to coordinate and advocate for policies to support families who are expecting or raising young children. The caucus will serve as a platform to elevate family-focused legislation and strengthen collaboration
“Strong families are essential to Pennsylvania’s economic future,”
said Senator Pisciottano
. “We want people to be able to afford to start a family here. When the cost of childcare makes it difficult for parents to stay in the workforce, or financial pressures cause couples to put off having children, those challenges have consequences for our economy. We need to make Pennsylvania a place where families have the support they need to grow and thrive.”
The caucus grew out of collaboration among the four legislators, who recognized an opportunity to bring their work on individual policy initiatives together under one umbrella and establish a more coordinated approach. While their experiences raising young children helped inspire the caucus, its mission extends beyond individual households. Policies that make it easier to raise a family strengthen the Commonwealth’s economy and improve its long-term outlook.
“Hardworking families drive this Commonwealth forward. In turn, our state legislature must do everything we can to guarantee parents – and those looking to grow their families – can comfortably and confidently raise the next generation of leaders, innovators, and engaged members of our communities,”
said Senator Cappelletti
. “As a legislator serving thousands of families across my district, and as a mom raising two young daughters, I’m proud to serve on a caucus that shows Pennsylvania families their lived experiences are being brought to the table in Harrisburg. They deserve nothing short of seeing their priorities be truly heard and turned into sustainable action.”
“As a husband, father, and legislator – I don’t just live a political life, I put my life into my politics,”
Representative Abney said
. “The Kids and Families Caucus is an opportunity to elevate pragmatic policies that help to improve the quality of life for many Pennsylvanians. I look forward to working with my colleagues to build upon the recent legislative wins giving kids and and families the tools needed to succeed in today’s economy.”
“Right now, parents and families are struggling to make ends meet,”
said Representative O’Mara
. “We hear every day about their struggles – from affording childcare to rising utility bills. I’m proud to be a part of this caucus so we can collectively advocate for legislation that will support Pennsylvanians as they grow and raise their family.”
The caucus will build on existing legislative efforts to address issues affecting Pennsylvania families, with an emphasis on bringing greater attention to proposals already under consideration and strengthening cooperation among lawmakers to move those initiatives forward.
“Over the past four years, the Shapiro-Davis Administration has made major investments to support working families with young children,”
said Lieutenant Governor Austin Davis
. “There is so much more to be done to support kids and families in Pennsylvania, and that’s why this caucus is so important. This is just the beginning.”
“Every family deserves the time and support to care for a new baby without having to choose between their health and their paycheck,”
said Allegheny County Executive Sara Innamorato
. “At Allegheny County, we’re working to make that a reality through our paid parental leave initiative, because supporting parents and babies is both a public health priority and an investment in our communities. I’m grateful to Senator Pisciottano and his colleagues for launching the Kids and Families Caucus and bringing renewed focus to the policies Pennsylvania families need, from paid leave and affordable childcare to maternal health and family affordability. By working together across all levels of government, we can build a Commonwealth where working families have more stability, more opportunities, and the support they need to thrive.”
Following the announcement, officials toured the Sampson Family YMCA’s childcare facilities to highlight the importance of accessible care and the role of state support in strengthening these services across Pennsylvania.
The Kids & Families Caucus will continue working with lawmakers, community organizations, and stakeholders to identify legislative priorities and advance policies that support children, parents, and families.

The caucus held a launch event at a YMCA in Plum, PA, attended by the Lieutenant Governor and Allegheny County Executive. No specific legislation was introduced or passed; the caucus is an organizing structure intended to prioritize issues like childcare affordability and family economic support.
